Rashi on Megillah 3b:10:1.hebrew: את לא תעשה - דכתיב לא תוכל להתעלם (דברים כ״ב:ג׳), וכתיב והתעלמת — פעמים שאתה מתעלם, כגון זקן ואינו לפי כבודו:
Rashi on Megillah 3b:10:1.english: A negative commandment - For it is written: "You shall not be able to ignore [it]" (Deuteronomy 22:3), and it is written: "and you shall ignore [them]" — [there are] times that you may ignore [it], such as [in the case of] an elder and it is not in accordance with his dignity.

Rashi on Megillah 3b:12:1.english: In a valley - A low place.

Rashi on Megillah 3b:13:1.hebrew: שישב ולבסוף הוקף - שנתיישב תחלה בבתים, ולבסוף הוקף חומה — נידון ככפר לענין בתי ערי חומה:
Rashi on Megillah 3b:13:1.english: That was settled and only later surrounded - That it was first settled with houses, and only later surrounded by a wall — it is judged like a village regarding [the law of] houses of walled cities.

Rashi on Megillah 3b:13:2.english: A dwelling house in a walled city - [That is,] a dwelling house of a walled city.

Rashi on Megillah 3b:14:1.hebrew: עשרה בטלנין - שבטלין ממלאכתן, שיהו מצויין תמיד בבית הכנסת שחרית וערבית, כדאמרינן במסכת ברכות (דף ו:): כיון שבא הקב"ה בבית הכנסת ולא מצא שם עשרה וכו':
Rashi on Megillah 3b:14:1.english: Ten idlers - Who are idle from their work so that they will always be present in the synagogue morning and evening, as we say in Tractate Berakhot (6b): "When the Holy One, Blessed be He, comes to the synagogue and does not find ten there, etc."

Rashi on Megillah 3b:14:2.english: We learned - In our chapter, in the Mishnah (daf 5a).

Rashi on Megillah 3b:14:3.hebrew: כרך איצטריכא ליה - דכל כרך אינו אלא מקום שווקין שנכנסים שם מכל צד, וגדול הוא יותר מעיר גדולה:
Rashi on Megillah 3b:14:3.english: It was necessary for him [to state regarding] a metropolis - For every metropolis is nothing other than a place of markets where [people] enter from every side, and it is larger than a large city.

Rashi on Megillah 3b:14:4.hebrew: דמיקלעי ליה מעלמא - אנשים הרבה, ויש הרבה מהן בטלין ממלאכ', שאין עושין מלאכה אלא במקומן. אפילו הכי, בעינן קבועין, דזמנין דלא משתכחין:
Rashi on Megillah 3b:14:4.english: That they happen to come to it from elsewhere - Many people, and many of them are idle from work, as they do not do work except in their [own] place. Even so, we require permanent [residents], for sometimes they are not found.

Rashi on Megillah 3b:15:1.english: [If] it was settled, yes - That it was surrounded [by a wall] once again.

Rashi on Megillah 3b:2:1.english: This [refers to] the public - For there, all of Israel were [present].

Rashi on Megillah 3b:3:1.english: [They] lament - A eulogy for the deceased.

Rashi on Megillah 3b:3:3.hebrew: אבל לא מקוננות - והתם מפרש איזהו עינוי ואיזהו קינה: עינוי — שכולן עונות כאחת; קינה — אחת אומרת וכולן עונות אחריה:
Rashi on Megillah 3b:3:3.english: But they may not lament - And there [in Moed Katan 28b] it explains what is innui and what is kinah: Innui is when all of them chant in unison; kinah is when one speaks and all of them respond after her.

Rashi on Megillah 3b:5:1.english: Torah study of an individual - The interruption of his study is lighter than Temple service and Purim.

Rashi on Megillah 3b:6:1.english: From [the teaching of] Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina - For he expounded, “[Every] family,” etc.

Rashi on Megillah 3b:8:1.hebrew: ולאחותו מה ת"ל - גבי נזיר כתיב: ״על נפש מת לא יבא״ (במדבר ו׳:ז׳) — הרי הכל במשמע. הדר כתיב בתריה קרא יתירא: ״לאביו ולאמו לאחיו ולאחותו״ כו׳. דריש לה בספרי: ״לאביו״ — לא יטמא, אבל מיטמא הוא למת מצוה. ״לאמו״ מה ת"ל? שאם היה כהן ונזיר, אע"פ שקדוש ב' קדושות — לאמו לא יטמא, אבל מיטמא הוא למת מצוה. ״לאחיו״ — שאם היה כהן גדול ונזיר, לאחיו לא יטמא, אבל מיטמא הוא למת מצוה, דעל כרחך כולהו למעוטי מת מצוה אתו. הלכך, אם אינו ענין לו, תנהו ענין לחבירו. ״ולאחותו מה ת"ל״ כו׳ — ואם אינו ענין לאלו, תנהו ענין לענין ביטול עבודה ומילה מפני מת מצוה:
Rashi on Megillah 3b:8:1.english: "And for his sister," what does the verse teach? - Regarding a nazirite it is written: "He shall not come near any dead body" (Numbers 6:7) — this already implies everyone. Then an extra verse is written after it: "For his father, or for his mother, for his brother, or for his sister..." etc. [The Sages] expound this in the Sifrei: "For his father" — he may not become impure [for him], but he does become impure for a *met mitzvah* [an unattended corpse]. What does "for his mother" teach? That if he was a priest and a nazirite, even though he is consecrated with two sanctities, for his mother he may not become impure, but he does become impure for a *met mitzvah*. "For his brother" — that if he was a High Priest and a nazirite, for his brother he may not become impure, but he does become impure for a *met mitzvah*, for perforce, all of them come to exclude a *met mitzvah*. Therefore, if it is not needed for its own matter, apply it to another matter. [Hence the baraita asks:] "What does 'and for his sister' teach?" etc. — and if it is not needed for these [matters], apply it to the matter of overriding [Temple] service and circumcision on account of a *met mitzvah*.

Rashi on Megillah 3b:8:2.english: That a relative died to him - A brother or a sister.

Rashi on Megillah 3b:9:1.hebrew: אמרת לא יטמא - כשם שאין נזיר מבטל נזירותו ליטמא לקרוביו, כך הוא זה לא יבטל מפסחו:
Rashi on Megillah 3b:9:1.english: You said: He shall not become impure - Just as a nazirite does not nullify his naziriteship to become impure for his relatives, so too, this [person] shall not desist from his Paschal offering.

Tosafot on Megillah 3b:13:1.hebrew: כרך שישב ולבסוף הוקף נדון ככפר - פירש הקונטרס דלענין בתי ערי חומה איירי, וה"נ משמע מדאייתי קרא ד"כי ימכור". וקשה: דאם כן, בערכין (דף לב.) הו"ל להש"ס למתני גבי הא דתני שאר דיני דבתי ערי חומה! ועוד קשה: דאם כן, הל"ל "נדון כערי החצרים", דשייך גבייהו! לכ"נ דלענין מגילה מיירי. מכל מקום, מייתי קרא ד"כי ימכור" לאשמועינן דחומה דמתנינן גבי מגילה — בכה"ג דמהני גבי ערי חומה, דהיינו הוקף ולבסוף ישב, כדכתיב: "בית מושב עיר חומה", דמשמע שנתיישב בתוך החומה. ואם תאמר: לקמן (מגילה דף ה:) אמרינן דטבריא שימה חומתה, אע"ג דאין לה דין ערי חומה, מ"מ קורין את המגילה בט"ו, דהם מוקפין חומה, כיון דמגניא מאויבים; וה"נ היה לנו לומר כשישב ולבסוף הוקף, כיון דמכסיא ומגניא? וי"ל: דשאני טבריא, דכיון דחזינן דהיקף ים מהני כהיקף חומה לגבי מגילה, גם כן דין הוא שיקראו המגילה בט"ו, שהרי היקף שלה קודם לישובה, והוי כשאר היקף דמהני בבתי ערי חומה; אבל ישב ולבסוף הוקף, לא מצינו בשום מקום דחשיב חומה שלה. וא"ת: לקמן בפרקין (שם) דקאמר: "אשר לו חומה" — פרט לשור אגר, פי': שאגרות חומות שלה, כגון שהבתים מדובקים יחד בעגול והוי כמו חומה סביב לעיר; ולמה לי קרא? תיפוק ליה דה"ל ישב ולבסוף הוקף, שהרי לא נגמרה חומת העיר עד שנגמרו כל הבתים! ויש לומר: דקרא אתא לאשמועינן דאפילו היכא דקים לן שלא דר אדם שם עד שנגמרו כל הבתים, אפילו הכי לא חשיב היקף. וצריך לומר: דהא דקאמר "נדון ככפר", מיירי דליכא י' בטלנים; דאי יש שם עשרה בטלנין, אמאי גרע מעיירות גדולות דהוו בי"ד:
Tosafot on Megillah 3b:13:1.english: "A walled city that was settled and only later surrounded [by a wall] is judged like a village" - Rashi explained that this refers to the matter of houses in walled cities, and this is also indicated by [the Gemara] citing the verse: "If a man sells [a residential house in a walled city]" (Leviticus 25:29). And it is difficult: for if so, in Arakhin (32a), the Gemara should have taught [this statement] alongside where it teaches the other laws of houses in walled cities! And furthermore, it is difficult: for if so, it should have said "is judged like open villages [arei hachatzerim]," which is [the term] relevant to them! Therefore, it appears that it is referring to the Megillah [reading]. Nevertheless, [the Gemara] cites the verse "when [a man] sells" to teach us that the wall we require regarding the Megillah must be of the type that is effective regarding walled cities — namely, that it was surrounded [by a wall] and only later settled, as it is written: "a dwelling house in a walled city" (Leviticus 25:29), which implies that it was settled inside the wall. And if you will say: Later (Megillah 5b) we say that regarding Tiberias, its sea is its wall; even though it does not have the legal status of walled cities, nevertheless they read the Megillah on the fifteenth, as they are surrounded by a wall, since it protects from enemies — and so too should we say when it was settled and only later surrounded, since it shelters and protects [from enemies]? And one can say: Tiberias is different, for since we see that an encirclement by the sea is effective like an encirclement by a wall regarding the Megillah, it is likewise logical that they should read the Megillah on the fifteenth, for its encirclement preceded its settlement, and thus it is like any other encirclement that is effective for houses in walled cities. But where it was settled and only later surrounded, we have found nowhere that its wall is considered [valid]. And if you will say: Later in our chapter (ibid.), where [the Gemara] says: "'Which has a wall' — excluding a wall of roofs [shur ager]," meaning that its roofs are its walls, such as when houses are joined together in a circle and serve like a wall around the city — why do I need a verse [to exclude this]? Let it be derived from the fact that it is [a case of] settled and only later surrounded, for the wall of the city was not completed until all the houses were completed! And one can say: The verse comes to teach us that even where it is clear to us that no person lived there until all the houses were completed, even so it is not considered an encirclement [by a wall]. And it must be said that that which [Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi] says, "is judged like a village," is dealing with [a case where] there are not ten idle men; for if there were ten idle men there, why would it be worse than large towns, which [read] on the fourteenth?

Tosafot on Megillah 3b:14:1.hebrew: כרך שאין בו י' בטלנים נדון ככפר - וצ"ל דמיירי בסתם כרכים האמורים בתלמוד. אבל המוקף חומה מימות יהושע בן נון — אפילו אין בו י' בטלנים, קורין בט"ו. וה"נ משמע, דפריך בסמוך: "מאי קמ"ל? תנינא: איזו היא עיר גדולה כו'", ומשני: "כרך איצטריך ליה, אע"ג דמקלעי ליה מעלמא". ואי איתא דאפילו במוקף חומה מימות יהושע בן נון צריך י' בטלנין, הוה ליה למימר: "מוקף מימות יהושע אצטריכא ליה, אע"ג דחשיב חומה דידהו שהגינו מן האויבים וגם מקלעי ליה מעלמא", דהוי רבותא טפי. אלא ש"מ, דבמוקף מימות יהושע לא צריך י':
Tosafot on Megillah 3b:14:1.english: "A kerakh that does not have ten idlers is judged like a village" - And it must be said that [this statement] is dealing with ordinary kerakhim mentioned throughout the Talmud. However, [a city] surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua the son of Nun, even if it does not have ten idlers, they read [the Megillah] on the fifteenth. And so it is also implied [from the fact] that [the Gemara] challenges nearby: "What does he teach us? We [already] learned: 'What is a large city? etc.,'" and answers: "It was necessary for him [to state this regarding] a kerakh, even though [people] happen to come to it from elsewhere." For if it were so, that even in [a city] surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua the son of Nun one requires ten idlers, [the Gemara] should have said: "It was necessary for him [to state this regarding a city] surrounded [by a wall] from the days of Joshua, even though its wall is considered [significant] because it protected [them] from enemies, and also [people] happen to come to it from elsewhere" — which would be an even greater novelty! Rather, conclude from this that in [a city] surrounded [by a wall] from the days of Joshua, ten [idlers] are not required.

Tosafot on Megillah 3b:15:1.hebrew: והתניא רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי אומר וכו' - וא"ת: אדמותבת ליה מרבי אליעזר, לסייעיה מרבנן דפליגי עליה, וסברי דקדושה ראשונה קדשה לשעתה ולא לעתיד לבא! ויש לומר: דע"כ לא סבר רבי יהושע כרבנן, דאי סבר כוותייהו, מאי מהני (. ישב ולבסוף הוקף) אם לא קדשה קדושה שנייה:
Tosafot on Megillah 3b:15:1.english: "And isn't it taught [in a baraita]: Rabbi Eliezer bar Yosei says, etc." - And if you will say: Rather than objecting to him from [the baraita of] Rabbi Eliezer, let [the Gemara] support him from the Rabbis who disagree with him and hold that the first sanctification sanctified [the Land] for its time, but did not sanctify [it] for the future to come! And one can say: Perforce, Rabbi Yehoshua does not hold in accordance with the Rabbis, for if he held in accordance with them, what would it avail (that it was settled and only later surrounded) if the second sanctification did not sanctify [it]?

Tosafot on Megillah 3b:16:1.hebrew: אלא שחרב מעשרה בטלנים - וכשלא הוקף מימות יהושע איירי, דביה לא צריך עשרה. ואם תאמר: מאי מהני מה שהיה כרך מתחילה? הוה ליה כפר שנעשה כרך שנתישבו שם עשרה! ויש לומר: דלרבותא נקט הכי — ולא מבעיא כפר שנעשה כרך, דבסתמא ליכא למיחש שמא יחסרו דיורים; אלא אפילו זה, שפסקו דיורים כבר פעם אחת, וסלקא דעתך אמינא דאיכא למיחש שמא יפסקו עוד פעם אחרת — אפילו הכי קא משמע לן דלא חיישינן:
Tosafot on Megillah 3b:16:1.english: "Rather, that it was destroyed of ten idlers" - And [Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi] is speaking of [a city] that was not walled from the days of Yehoshua [bin Nun], for in that [case of one walled from the days of Yehoshua], it does not require ten [idlers]. And if you say: What difference does it make that it was originally a metropolis? It is [no different from] a village that became a metropolis when ten [idlers] settled there! And one can say that it formulated [the case] this way for greater novelty: and [the meaning is,] not only [is it true of] a village that became a metropolis, where ordinarily there is no concern that residents will be lacking; but even this [city], where residents already ceased [dwelling] once, and it might enter your mind to say that there is concern lest they cease yet again — even so, it teaches us that we do not have [such] a concern.

Tosafot on Megillah 3b:1:1.hebrew: מלמד שהלך ולן בעומקה של הלכה - "כל זמן ששכינה וארון שרויין שלא במקומן אסורים בתשמיש המטה" — לא גרס ליה הכא, דמה שייך כאן? ובפרק הדר (עירובין סג:) גרס ליה, דקאמר שנענש יהושע על שבטל ישראל מפריה ורביה. י"ל: דמה שנענש שלא היה לו בן זכר היה על שבטל ישראל מתשמיש — מדה כנגד מדה; אבל שאר עונש בא לו על בטול תורה:
Tosafot on Megillah 3b:1:1.english: "This teaches that he went and spent the night in the depths of halakha" - [The text,] "As long as the Divine Presence and the Ark are situated not in their place, they are forbidden from marital relations," should not be read here, for what relevance does it have here? And in the chapter [entitled] "Hadar" (Eruvin 63b), it is read, as it says [there] that Joshua was punished for causing Israel to neglect procreation. One can say that [the fact] that he was punished by not having a male child was because he caused Israel to neglect marital relations — measure for measure; but the rest of the punishment came upon him for neglecting Torah study.

Tosafot on Megillah 3b:3:1.hebrew: מענות - כולן עונות כאחת. מקוננות — אחת אומרת, והשאר עונות. מטפחות — יד על יד, או על ירך, או על פנים:
Tosafot on Megillah 3b:3:1.english: "[Women] may wail" - All of them wail together as one. "They lament" [mekonenot] — one speaks, and the rest respond. "They clap" [metapeḥot] — [striking] hand against hand, or on the thigh, or on the face.

Tosafot on Megillah 3b:4:1.english: "There is no Festival in the presence of a Torah scholar" - And the day of [receiving the] report is considered like [being] in his presence.

Tosafot on Megillah 3b:4:2.hebrew: כל שכן חנוכה ופורים - שמותר להספידם, אע"ג דמבטל ממקרא מגילה — אלמא ת"ת חמור ממקרא מגילה:
Tosafot on Megillah 3b:4:2.english: "All the more so Hanukkah and Purim" - That it is permitted to eulogize them [Torah scholars], even though it causes neglect of the reading of the Megillah — evidently, Torah study is more stringent than the reading of the Megillah.

Tosafot on Megillah 3b:7:1.hebrew: מת מצוה עדיף - לאו דווקא מת מצוה, והוא הדין לכל מתים שבעולם — מבטלים תלמוד תורה להוציאם; אלא איידי דנקט בסמוך גבי "ולאחותו" מת מצוה, ה"נ נקט תלמוד תורה ומת מצוה:
Tosafot on Megillah 3b:7:1.english: "A met mitzvah takes precedence" - [This is] not specifically [true of] a met mitzvah [an unattended corpse], for the same applies to all dead in the world — one suspends Torah study to take them out [for burial]. Rather, since [the Gemara] mentions nearby, regarding "or for his sister," a met mitzvah, here too it stated: "Torah study and a met mitzvah."

Tosafot on Megillah 3b:7:2.hebrew: מת מצוה עדיף - הקשה הר"ר אלחנן: למה לי קרא? תיפוק ליה מק"ו: ומה ת"ת דחמירא מבטלין משום כבוד המת, עבודה דקילא לא כל שכן? דהא אפילו תלמוד תורה דרבים מבטלין משום כבוד המת, כדאמר פ"ב דכתובות (דף יז ושם). וי"ל: דה"מ למאן דקרי ותני ומתני, דצריך כולי האי; אבל למאן דלא קרי ותני, לא צריך כולי האי. והכא מיירי במת מצוה דלא קרי ותני, ומשום הכי צריך קרא דולאחותו:
Tosafot on Megillah 3b:7:2.english: "A met mitzvah takes precedence" - Rabbeinu Elchanan raised a difficulty: Why do I need a verse? Let it be derived from an a fortiori argument [kal va-chomer]: If Torah study, which is stringent, is suspended for the honor of the deceased, shouldn't [Temple] service, which is lenient, all the more so [be suspended]? For even public Torah study is suspended for the honor of the deceased, as [the Gemara] states in the second chapter of Ketubot (17a and there [17b]). And it can be answered: This applies only to one who read [Scripture], studied [Mishnah], and taught [others], for whom all this [honor] is required; but for one who did not read and study, all this is not required. And here, we are dealing with a met mitzvah who did not read and study, and for that reason the verse "or for his sister" is needed.
